quizzes.title: Engines, Stages and Materials
quizzes.passage: Vikram-1 is India's first privately built orbital launch vehicle. Skyroot Aerospace, a Hyderabad-based company, developed it, and the rocket flew its maiden mission, named Mission Aagaman, from the Satish Dhawan Centre at Sriharikota. The flight placed payloads into Low Earth Orbit. With it, India became the third country, after the United States and China, to demonstrate private orbital launch capability. The booklet gives close attention to the rocket's propulsion and structure, covering its stages, engines and materials. The rocket also carries a mix of payloads. The booklet describes them as scientific, technological, commercial and symbolic, and lists them together on one manifest. Among the technology items is SCOPE, which validates onboard spacecraft systems during the flight. Authorisation and facilitation for the launch came from IN-SPACe, which functions as a single-window regulator for private space activities. The Indian Space Policy 2023 opened the complete space value chain to non-government entities, which the booklet calls a fundamental transformation of India's space ecosystem. The mission follows Vikram-S, India's first privately developed sub-orbital rocket. A sub-orbital rocket goes to space but does not place a satellite into orbit, which is the key difference from an orbital rocket. The booklet is a July 2026 current affairs publication on defence, space and science and technology.

questions.q: What does SOrTeD stand for in the name Agnibaan SOrTeD?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that SOrTeD stands for SubOrbital Technology Demonstrator.

questions.q: Which company developed Agnibaan SOrTeD?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Agnikul Cosmos as the developer of Agnibaan SOrTeD.

questions.q: Vikram-1 is a how-many-stage orbital launch vehicle?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes Vikram-1 as a 4-stage orbital launch vehicle.

questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because Agnikul Cosmos developed Agnibaan SOrTeD, while I and III match the booklet.

questions.explanation: Only statement III is correct, since Vikram-1 has four stages and the Kalam Engines use advanced solid propellants.

Its maiden flight, Mission Aagaman, took off from the Satish Dhawan Centre at Sriharikota. An orbital rocket places a satellite into orbit around Earth. A sub-orbital rocket, by contrast, goes to space but does not place a satellite into orbit. Vikram-1 is an orbital vehicle, while Vikram-S, which it follows, was India's first privately developed sub-orbital rocket. The launch placed payloads into Low Earth Orbit, and India became the third country, after the United States and China, to demonstrate private orbital launch capability. The booklet's coverage of the mission includes the rocket's propulsion and structure, discussed across its stages, engines and materials. The vehicle's payloads are classed as scientific, technological, commercial and symbolic, and they are listed together on a single manifest. IN-SPACe authorised and facilitated the launch, and the booklet describes it as a single-window regulator for private space activities. The Indian Space Policy 2023 opened the complete space value chain to non-government entities. The booklet is a July 2026 current affairs publication covering defence, space and science and technology, and this section forms part of its space coverage. The Vikram-1 section is headed Why in News.

questions.explanation: The booklet calls Agnibaan SOrTeD the world's first rocket with a fully 3D-printed engine.
